doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Highlight: Haggart and Lawson band and Emporium of Jazz tape
summary: He loved the Haggart-Lawson band and recalls a tape from the Emporium of Jazz near Minneapolis.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Is there a particular gig, or series of gigs that you can remember that was like, man, one of the real highlights of your career?
Well I enjoyed playing with Bob Haggart and Yank Lawson in that band. That was a good band.
Yeah. It just about lived up to the title of that band.
Right. But we didn’t give it that title.

But we had a great band. And a guy sent me a tape, a cassette, from Minneapolis. We played in a place, oh this goes back to the early ‘70s. And we played a place outside of Minneapolis, called the Emporium of Jazz. And the band was Benny Morton on trombone, Yank Lawson, Billy Butterfield, Bud Freeman, Bob Wilber, Gus Johnson on drums, Bob Haggart and myself. And he recorded it one night when we were playing in there. And he sent me this tape. And I hadn’t heard it. And I’m going to the airport with my wife. We put the thing in and played this, and I couldn’t believe it man, it gave me goose pimples.
